title: Microbiologically Induced Calcite Precipitation Mediated by Sporosarcina pasteurii
protocol: Assemble equipment and ingredients such as Petri dishes, flask, Tris-base, HCl, agar, Millipore water, pH-meter etc.
Sterilize all containers by autoclaving at 121 °C before use.
Prepare 1 L of 0.13 M aqueous solution of Tris-buffer by mixing 15.75 g Tris-base with 1 L of Millipore water.
Add 2,800 µl of HCl (50% concentration) to lower the pH level of the original solution (pH 10.4).
Check continuously using a pH-meter to set pH = 9.
Divide the 1 L buffer solution into two parts as follows: Take 800 ml of this solution and divide it equally into two parts of 400 ml each.
Dissolve 8 g (NH4)2SO4 in one part and 16 g yeast extract in the other part.
Take the remaining (200 ml of) solution and divide it again into two parts of 100 ml each.
Mix 2 g (NH4)2SO4 to one part.
Add 4 g yeast extract and 4 g agar to the other part.
Autoclave the 4 solutions separately.
Wrap the respective flasks in aluminum foil.
Stick autoclave tapes to the wrapped flasks.
Set the volume of the benchtop autoclave unit to 500 ml if used.
Take out the solutions after autoclaving.
Set aside two 400 ml solutions for step 1.3.1.
Mix the two 100 ml solutions to create a 200 ml solution.
Pour the mixture into 10-12 Petri dishes.
Remove bacterial stock from freezer at -80 °C.
Allow bacterial stock to thaw properly.
Place bacterial stock and agar plate inside a biosafety hood.
Select micropipette with smallest available dimension (0.5 - 10 µl).
Infest the tip of the micropipette with Sporosarcina pasteurii stock.
Streak an agar plate using the micropipette tip.
Place streaked agar plate inside a non-shaking incubator at 31 °C.
Incubate for 48 hours.
Remove plate from incubator after 48 hours.
Visually examine plate for single colonies.
If no single colonies are present, return to incubator for another 24 hours.
Repeat the process until single colonies are detected or up to 7 days total.
Do not exceed 7 days of trial.
If single colonies do not appear even after a week, repeat the entire process from step 1.
Mix 400 ml of Tris buffer + (NH4)2SO4 with 400 ml of Tris buffer + yeast extract.
Transfer 125 ml of the mixed solution into a flask.
Identify regions with high concentration of single colonies on the surface of the agar plate.
Gently break one colony with a micropipette tip.
Dip the micropipette tip containing broken colony cells into the 125 ml flask and stir thoroughly.
Place the flask in a shaking incubator at 150 rpm, 30 °C for 2 - 3 days.
Remove the flask from the incubator after 2 - 3 days.
Perform serial dilution of the non-diluted culture solution using PBS to attain a dilution of at least ten million (10-7).
Draw seven parallel equidistant lines on one of the agar plates.
Drop 3 little drops of non-diluted solution into one segment on the agar plate.
Add 1 ml of non-diluted solution to 9 ml of Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) to obtain a 1:10 dilution.
Take a small aliquot (~ 0.1 ml) of this newly diluted solution and drop 3 more small drops on the next segment.
Transfer the newly diluted solution to a new flask and further dilute ten times by adding PBS.
This brings down the dilution to 10-2 or 1:100.
Use a 1:100 solution in the next segment.
Repeat this process with small volumes of freshly diluted solutions by successively transferring them to new flasks and continuously diluting ten-fold (10x) in tandem with PBS.
Dilute samples from 10-3 or 1:1,000 all the way down to 10-7 or 1:1,000,000 into the last segment.
Perform Colony-Forming Unit (CFU) plate count after incubating the plate for 1 - 2 days at 31 °C.
Seal the Petri dishes with self-sealing film.
Store remaining items in a refrigerator for future use.
Transfer 9 ml of the prepared culture liquid (cells + medium) into several sterilized centrifuge tubes, each of 10 ml volume.
Prepare a stock solution of external enrichment in fresh medium.
Measure 2 g/L urea, 1 g/L ammonium chloride, 212 mg/L sodium bicarbonate, and 280 mg/L calcium chloride using an analytical balance.
Mix ammonium chloride, sodium bicarbonate, and calcium chloride with fresh medium in a beaker.
Place the mixture in the autoclave (121 °C, 15 psi, 15 min).
Remove the autoclaved solution from the autoclave.
Add 2 mg of urea to 1 ml of fresh medium.
Pass the mixture through a syringe fitted with a 0.22 µm filter.
Mix 1 ml of enriched medium with 9 ml of prepared culture liquid in sterilized centrifuge tubes.
Vortex each tube thoroughly using a mechanical vortexer.
Place the enriched liquids (cells + medium + additives) in a non-shaking incubator at 30 °C.
Monitor units regularly for initiation of precipitation.
Begin microscopic observations once onset of precipitation is detected with the naked eye, usually between 30 - 36 hours after start of experiments.
Transfer approximately 1 ml of fluid to a high-magnification microscopy-chambered coverglass system for initial observations.
Start all observations with the lowest magnification (4X).
Select particular areas with significant volumes of precipitations and zoom in using 20X magnification.
Further increase magnification to 40X to examine specific areas closely.
Continue increasing magnification to 60X for detailed observations.
Switch to phase-contrast mode when necessary to differentiate cell membranes from the EPS.
Stain some chambers with Live/Dead stain to selectively dye live components green and dead components red.
Switch on fluorescent mode.
Use the red filter cube with Excitation wavelength of 540 - 580 nm, Dichroic mirror of 595 nm, and Barrier filter of 600 - 660 nm for red regions.
Use the GFP Long-pass Green filter cube with Excitation wavelength of 440 - 480 nm, Dichroic mirror of 505 nm, and Barrier filter of 510 nm for green regions.
Select the best images from multi-mode data.
Manually overlay individual brightfield, phase-contrast, and fluorescent images to achieve optimal contrast and clarity.
Perform SEM on dried solid samples to understand crystal structures.
Perform XPS to identify chemical signatures of functional groups (carbonates).
